The Department of Animal Sciences and Agricultural Education offers degrees with options in Agricultural Communication, Teacher Preparation, and various Animal Science options. The Animal Science option has career specialization in the areas of Pre-Professional Animal Science and Pre-Veterinary Medicine. While the Animal Science production management option offers career specialization in Dairy Science, Equine Science, Meat Technology, as well as Livestock and Poultry Management. Our Animal Science curriculum integrates various topics, such as: animal evaluation, behavior, disease, genetics, health, reproduction, environmental management, marketing, muscle biology, nutrition, and physiology.


Advising Notes

CR/NC grading is not permitted for courses included in the major unless the courses have been designated as CR/NC only.

Total number of units will exceed 120 if a student chooses to meet all of the Veterinary Medicine entrance requirements. Preveterinary and veterinary preparation students should consult their faculty advisor regarding entrance requirements and admissions procedures to veterinary school. Additional courses such as PHYS 2B, calculus, and statistics may be required.

  1. Mandatory advising is required of all students in the degree program. See the administrative support coordinator for the name of your assigned advisor.
  2. New students should request an option advising check sheet from the department office.
  3. All students should make an appointment with their assigned faculty advisor prior to registration each semester.


In addition to the major program requirements, every student must also complete the University’s baccalaureate degree requirements such as:

  • American Government and Institutions (PLSI 2)
  • General Education Requirements (43 units)
  • Additional University Graduation Requirements (9 units) - Animal Science - Science - Preprofessional majors are exempt from 3 units of this requirement. Students with a declared Animal Science - Science - Preprofessional major following a TMC/ADT similar pathway are fully exempt from this degree requirement.
  • Upper-Division Writing Requirement
  • Sufficient Elective Units to Meet Required Total Units (varies); it is recommended that units in this area be utilized to complete a second major or minor.

A full description of the University’s graduation requirements can be found in the Baccalaureate Degree Requirements.

Additional University Graduation Requirements


The Additional University Graduation Requirements are designed to complement the GE requirements. It is the policy of Fresno State, that all students will cultivate and refine their affective, cognitive, and physical faculties through studying great works of the human imagination; be equipped for lifelong understanding and development of themselves as integrated physiological, social, and psychological beings; and be prepared to understand and live in a multicultural and international world through their undergraduate education.

This will be accomplished through a total of 9 units from the following areas, each requiring 3 units:

  1. Arts/Humanities (A/H) - All students are required to take an Arts/Humanities course to graduate at the bachelor’s degree level. 
  2. Lifelong-Understanding and Self-Development (L/S) - All students are required to take a lifelong understanding and self-development course to for graduate at the bachelor’s degree level. 
  3. Multicultural/International (M/I) - All Students are required to take a Multicultural / International course at Fresno State to graduate at the bachelor’s degree level.
